questions.title: Intellectual property
questions.text: Define the term **intellectual property** and give **one** example.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Creations of the mind (non-physical) that the creator owns and has legal rights over (1)
- Example: software, a song, a book, a film, an invention, a logo / brand name (1)
scheme.model_answer: Creations of the mind, such as software or music, that belong to their creator, who has the legal right to control how they are used.

questions.title: Copyright, patent or trademark
questions.text: Tick (✓) **one** box in each row to show how each item is protected.

prefill: The source code of a mobile app
A new design of solar panel that produces more energy
A novel written by a student

scheme.mark_scheme: Source code → Copyright (1); Solar panel → Patent (1); Logo → Trademark (1); Novel → Copyright (1)

questions.title: Copyright vs patent
questions.text: Explain the difference between **copyright** and a **patent**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Copyright protects original works (code, text, music) and is automatic (1)
- A patent protects an invention / technical solution and must be applied for and registered (1)
scheme.model_answer: Copyright protects original works such as program code and arises automatically, whereas a patent protects an invention and must be registered.

questions.title: Copyright is automatic
questions.text: A photo on a website is free for anyone to use because it is on the Internet.

scheme.mark_scheme: False.
scheme.explanation: Copyright applies automatically; the photo can only be used with permission or under its licence.

questions.title: Software licences
questions.text: Match each type of licence to its description.

right.text: Must be paid for; copying and changing are not allowed
Free for a trial period, then must be paid for
Free to use, but the source code is not available
Free, and the source code can be studied and modified

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3, L4–R4. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Problems of piracy
questions.text: Analyse the problems that arise when people download pirated copies of computer games.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any three developed points (1 each): developers lose income / royalties; less money for new games / jobs; users break the law — fines; pirated copies may contain malware; no updates / support / online play; lost tax revenue; unethical — using work without paying
scheme.model_answer: The game company loses income, so it has less money to pay developers and make new games. People who download pirated copies break copyright law and may be fined, and the copies often contain malware that can steal their data.

questions.title: Plagiarism
questions.text: Explain what **plagiarism** is and how a student can avoid it in a research project.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Presenting someone else's work / ideas as your own without acknowledging the source (1)
- Avoid by citing sources / using quotation marks / paraphrasing in your own words with a reference / a bibliography (1)
scheme.model_answer: Plagiarism is presenting another person's work as your own. A student avoids it by putting quotations in quotation marks and citing every source in a reference list.

questions.title: Using an image legally
questions.text: State **two** ways a student can legally use an image from the Internet in a school website.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): ask the owner for permission; use Creative Commons / copyright-free images and follow the licence; credit / attribute the author; buy a licence (stock photo); create their own image
scheme.model_answer: 1 Use an image with a Creative Commons licence and credit the author. 2 Ask the photographer for permission.

questions.title: Creative Commons
questions.text: An image has the licence **CC BY-NC**. What may you do with it?

options.content: Sell it on T-shirts without credit
Use it in a school project with credit to the author
Claim it as your own work
Use it in a paid advertisement

scheme.mark_scheme: B
scheme.explanation: BY = give credit to the author; NC = non-commercial use only.

questions.title: Fake news
questions.text: Analyse the problems caused when false information about a medicine spreads on social media.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any three developed points (1 each): people may take a harmful treatment / avoid a safe one — health risk; spreads faster than corrections; panic / shortages; damages the reputation of doctors / companies; loss of trust in reliable sources; difficult to remove once shared
scheme.model_answer: People may stop taking a safe medicine or take a dangerous one, putting their health at risk. False posts spread much faster than corrections, so many people see them, and trust in doctors and reliable news sources falls.

questions.title: Check information
questions.text: State **two** ways to check whether information found online is reliable.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): check the author / source is known and reliable; compare with other reliable sources; check the date; use fact-checking websites; check the website address / domain; look for evidence / references
scheme.model_answer: 1 Compare it with other reliable sources. 2 Check who the author is and when it was published.

questions.title: Disseminating information
questions.text: Select **two** actions that are problems caused by disseminating information without permission.

options.content: Posting a classmate's phone number and address on social media
Citing a website in a bibliography
Uploading a new film to a file-sharing site
Using an open-source library according to its licence

scheme.mark_scheme: A and C. One mark each; a mark is lost for each incorrect option selected.

questions.title: E-government
questions.text: Describe what is meant by **e-government** and name the main e-government portal in Kazakhstan.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Providing public / state services to citizens and businesses online using the Internet (1)
- egov.kz / eGov mobile (1)
scheme.model_answer: The use of the Internet by the state to provide public services online; in Kazakhstan the portal is egov.kz.

questions.title: eGov services
questions.text: Give **three** services that a citizen can receive through egov.kz.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any three (1 each): certificates (address, no criminal record, birth / marriage); registration of residence / car / business; paying taxes / fines; applying to kindergarten / school; booking a doctor / attaching to a clinic; social benefits / pension information; digital documents; licences (elicense.kz)
scheme.model_answer: 1 Getting a certificate of address registration. 2 Paying a traffic fine. 3 Applying for a place in a kindergarten.

questions.title: Electronic digital signature
questions.text: Explain the purpose of an **electronic digital signature (EDS)** when using eGov services.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Confirms / proves the identity of the person signing (authentication) (1)
- shows that the document has not been changed after signing / has legal force like a handwritten signature (1)
scheme.model_answer: It proves that the application was signed by the citizen and not someone else, and shows that the document has not been changed after it was signed.

questions.title: Advantages and risks
questions.text: Tick (✓) **one** box in each row to show whether the statement is an advantage or a risk of e-government.

prefill: Services are available 24 hours a day
Fake websites may steal citizens' passwords
Fewer face-to-face meetings with officials reduce corruption
Elderly people without Internet skills cannot use the services

scheme.mark_scheme: 1 Advantage (1); 2 Risk (1); 3 Advantage (1); 4 Risk (1)

questions.title: Using eGov safely
questions.text: State **two** precautions a citizen should take when using eGov services.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): never share EDS password / SMS code; type egov.kz or use the official app — do not follow links in messages; check HTTPS and the address; log out on shared computers; keep the EDS file on a protected device
scheme.model_answer: 1 Never tell anyone the SMS code. 2 Type egov.kz into the browser instead of clicking links in messages.

questions.title: A school documentary
questions.text:
Students make a documentary about Almaty for a competition. They plan to use a popular song as background music, photos found with a search engine, and text copied from a travel website. The video will be published on YouTube.

Discuss the problems this could cause and how the students should use these materials.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Problems (max 2): copyright infringement for the song / photos — video removed / blocked, disqualification, fines; copied text is plagiarism; creators lose income / credit
Solutions (max 2): royalty-free / Creative Commons music; CC or own photos with attribution / permission; rewrite text in own words and cite the website; check licence conditions (non-commercial)
[Max 4]
scheme.model_answer: The song and photos are protected by copyright, so YouTube may block the video and the students could be disqualified or fined; copying text from the travel site is plagiarism. They should use royalty-free or Creative Commons music, take their own photos or use CC photos with credit to the authors, and write the text in their own words, citing the website.

questions.title: Evaluate e-government
questions.text: Evaluate the use of e-government services such as egov.kz for citizens of Kazakhstan. Refer to specific services, security and possible problems.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Services (max 2): specific examples with benefit
Advantages (max 2): 24/7, saves time and travel, less paperwork, less corruption, transparency, automatic data from state databases
Security (max 1): EDS, SMS codes, biometrics
Problems (max 2): digital divide, cyber-attacks / data leaks, phishing, technical failures
Conclusion (1)
[Max 6]
scheme.model_answer: On egov.kz citizens can get certificates, pay fines and apply to kindergartens online at any time, which saves queues and travel, especially for people far from offices. Fewer face-to-face contacts with officials also reduce corruption. Applications are signed with an electronic digital signature or a one-time SMS code, which confirms the citizen's identity. However, elderly people or those without Internet access may be unable to use the services, and fake eGov sites and messages are used to steal codes. A large state database is also a target for hackers. Overall e-government is very beneficial, provided citizens are taught to use it safely and offline help remains for those who need it.

questions.title: Protecting intellectual property
questions.text: A company in Astana develops a navigation app with its own logo and a new route-finding device.

parts.title: Type of protection
parts.text: Tick (✓) **one** box in each row to show how each item is protected.

prefill: The program code of the app

scheme.mark_scheme: Code → Copyright (1); Logo → Trademark (1); Device → Patent (1)

parts.title: Piracy
parts.text: Cracked copies of the paid version of the app appear on the Internet. Analyse the problems this causes.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any three developed points (1 each): company loses income; less investment in updates / jobs; users of cracked copies break the law; cracked copies may contain malware / steal location data; no updates / support; damage to reputation if malware is blamed on the app
scheme.model_answer: The company loses sales, so it has less money to improve the app and pay its programmers. Users of the cracked copies break copyright law, and the copies may contain malware that steals their location and personal data.

parts.title: Licences
parts.text: The company uses an **open-source** map library in its app. Explain how open-source software differs from **freeware**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Open source: the source code is available and can be studied / modified / redistributed under the licence (1)
- Freeware: free to use but the source code is not available / cannot be modified (1)
scheme.model_answer: Open-source software provides its source code, which can be modified and shared under the licence, whereas freeware is free to use but its code is closed and cannot be changed.

questions.title: Using information responsibly
questions.text: Students are preparing a presentation about climate change using information from the Internet.

parts.title: Plagiarism
parts.text: Explain what plagiarism is and how the students can avoid it.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Presenting others' work as one's own without acknowledgement (1)
- cite sources / quotation marks / paraphrase with references (1)
scheme.model_answer: Plagiarism is using someone else's work as if it were yours. The students should write in their own words and cite every source they use.

parts.title: Images
parts.text: State **two** ways the students can use photographs from the Internet legally.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): Creative Commons / copyright-free images following the licence; credit the author; ask permission; buy a licence
scheme.model_answer: 1 Use Creative Commons photos. 2 Credit the photographer.

parts.title: False information
parts.text: A video claiming that climate change is a hoax has millions of views. Analyse the problems caused by spreading such false information, and explain how the students can check whether a source is reliable.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Problems (max 2): people make wrong decisions / ignore real risks; spreads faster than corrections; reduces trust in scientists / media; influences policy / votes
Checking (max 2): author / organisation reliable; compare with scientific sources; check date and evidence / references; fact-checking sites; check the domain
scheme.model_answer: People who believe the video may ignore real dangers and oppose useful measures, and because false videos spread faster than corrections, trust in scientists falls. The students should check who made the video and compare its claims with reliable scientific sources and fact-checking sites.

questions.title: E-government
questions.text: Mr Seitkali needs a certificate of address registration for his son's school application.

parts.title: Services
parts.text: Apart from certificates, state **two** other services Mr Seitkali can use on egov.kz.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): pay taxes / fines; register a car / business / residence; apply to a school / kindergarten; book a doctor; social payments / pension; digital documents; licences
scheme.model_answer: 1 Paying a traffic fine. 2 Registering a car.

parts.title: EDS
parts.text: He signs the request with an electronic digital signature. Explain the purpose of the EDS.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Confirms his identity (1)
- shows the request has not been altered / gives it legal force (1)
scheme.model_answer: It proves that the request comes from Mr Seitkali and that it has not been changed after he signed it.

parts.title: Advantage
parts.text: Explain **one** advantage of receiving the certificate online instead of at a public service centre.

scheme.mark_scheme: Advantage (1) + explanation (1): available 24/7; no travel / queue — saves time; certificate arrives instantly as PDF with QR code; less corruption
scheme.model_answer: He does not need to travel or wait in a queue, because the certificate appears in his personal account within minutes, at any time of day.

parts.title: Risk
parts.text: He receives an SMS: *"Your eGov account is blocked. Click the link and enter your code."* Explain the risk and what he should do.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Phishing — a fake site to steal his code / password / EDS and access his account (1)
- He should not click the link / not share the code; go to egov.kz directly / contact the official support (1)
scheme.model_answer: It is probably phishing: the link leads to a fake site that steals his code. He should not click it and should log in only by typing egov.kz himself.

summary: Intellectual property and how it is protected (copyright, patents, trademarks, licences), the problems caused by disseminating and using information (piracy, plagiarism, misinformation, privacy breaches), and using e-government (eGov) resources safely.

blocks.content: Creations of the **mind** — inventions, software, books, music, films, designs, brand names and logos — that the **creator owns** and has the legal right to control, even though they are not physical objects.

blocks.title: Ways intellectual property is protected
rows: **Original works**: software code, texts, music, films, photos, websites
**Automatically** when the work is created; lasts the author's life + 70 years (in Kazakhstan and many countries)
The code of a mobile game; a song
**Applied for** and registered; lasts about 20 years
**Brand names, logos, slogans** that identify a company's products

blocks.title: The law in Kazakhstan
blocks.content: The **Law on Copyright and Related Rights** protects works including **computer programs and databases**. Intellectual property is also protected by the **Civil Code**, and serious infringement is a criminal offence.

blocks.title: Software licences
rows: Free for a **trial period**, then pay
Usually yes, but not change it
**Yes**, and you may **modify** it (under the licence terms, e.g. GPL)
Free, under conditions: attribution (BY), non-commercial (NC), no derivatives (ND), share-alike (SA)

theory.title: Problems caused by disseminating and using information

blocks.content: Digital information can be **copied and shared instantly, perfectly and almost free of charge**. This brings huge benefits, but also problems for creators, individuals and society.

blocks.title: Problems of disseminating and using information
rows: Copying, sharing or selling software, films, music or books **without permission**
Creators and companies lose **income**; less money for new products; users risk **malware** in pirated copies
Presenting someone else's work or ideas **as your own** without acknowledging the source
The original author; the plagiarist's learning and reputation; academic honesty
Using images, music or videos in a website or video without a licence
Creators; the user may be **fined** or have content removed
False or misleading information spreads quickly on social media
Public **health**, elections, trust in media; people make wrong decisions
Personal information is published or shared without consent (doxxing, leaked databases)
False statements that damage someone's reputation
Too much information of mixed quality
Users find it hard to decide what is **true**

items.title: Analysing a problem — piracy
items.content:
- **For the creator:** loss of sales and royalties; less money to pay developers.
- **For the user:** legal risk (fines), **no updates or support**, pirated copies often contain **malware**.
- **For society:** fewer new products, lower investment in the IT industry, lost tax revenue.
- **Ethically:** it is using someone else's work **without paying** for it.

items.title: Analysing a problem — fake news
items.content:
- Spreads **faster** than corrections because it is shocking or emotional.
- Can cause **panic**, damage reputations, influence **elections** or harm health (false cures).
- Makes people **distrust** all media, including reliable sources.
- **Solutions:** check the source, compare with other reliable sources, look at the date, use fact-checking sites, think before sharing.

blocks.title: How to use information legally and ethically
rows: Using a photo from the Internet in a project
Use **copyright-free / Creative Commons** images and **credit** the author, or ask permission
Quoting a book or website in an essay
Use **quotation marks** and **cite the source** (author, title, date, URL)
Buy a **licence** or use **free / open-source** alternatives
**Check** that it comes from a reliable source before sharing
Get their **consent**; do not share personal data

blocks.title: Fair use / exceptions
blocks.content: Copyright law allows limited use without permission for **education, criticism, news reporting and quotation**, as long as the source is acknowledged and only a **reasonable part** is used.

The use of the **Internet and digital technologies** by the state to provide **public services** to citizens and businesses **online**. In Kazakhstan the main portal is **egov.kz** with the **eGov mobile** app.

blocks.title: Examples of eGov services in Kazakhstan
columns: What the citizen can do online
rows: Get a certificate of address registration, no criminal record, birth or marriage certificate
Register a place of residence, a car, a business (individual entrepreneur)
Apply to a kindergarten or school, see UNT results, apply for grants
Attach to a clinic, book a doctor's appointment
Apply for benefits and pensions, check pension savings (ENPF)
Show an ID card or driving licence from the phone instead of the paper document

items.title: Logging in and signing securely
items.content:
- **Electronic digital signature (EDS / ЭЦП)** — a pair of keys stored as a file or on an ID card; it **proves the identity** of the person and **confirms** that a signed document has not been changed.
- **One-time SMS password** linked to the citizen's registered phone number (two-factor authentication).
- **Biometric** confirmation (face scan) in the eGov mobile app.

items.title: Steps to receive a service
items.content:
1. Log in to **egov.kz** with an EDS, password + SMS or eGov mobile.
2. Choose the service from the catalogue.
3. Fill in the online **application form** (much data is filled in automatically from state databases).
4. **Sign** the application with the EDS or SMS code.
5. Receive the result (e.g. a PDF certificate with a QR code) in your **personal account**.

blocks.title: Advantages and disadvantages of e-government
rows: Needs **Internet access**, a device and digital skills — the **digital divide** (elderly, rural areas)
Risk of **cyber-attacks** and leaks of citizens' personal data
**Less paperwork**; documents checked automatically between databases
**Phishing** — fake eGov sites and SMS messages that steal passwords or EDS
**Less corruption** — fewer face-to-face contacts with officials
**Transparent** — the citizen can track the status of an application
People may lose or share their EDS key and password

blocks.content:
- Type **egov.kz** yourself or use the official app — do not follow links in unexpected messages.
- **Never share** your EDS password or SMS codes with anyone (officials never ask for them).
- Keep the EDS file on a protected device and **log out** on shared computers.
- Check that the site uses **HTTPS** and the correct address.

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Analyse one problem that arises when software is copied illegally. [2]**
The developer **loses income** from sales (1), so it has less money to employ programmers and develop updates or new products; users of pirated copies also risk **malware** and get no support (1).

**Q: Explain the difference between copyright and a patent. [2]**
Copyright protects **original works** such as software code and texts and is **automatic** (1); a patent protects an **invention** and must be **applied for and registered** (1).

**Q: Give two advantages of using e-government services. [2]**
Services are available **24/7** without visiting an office (1); **saves time** / no queues / less paperwork / less corruption (1).

**Q: Explain the purpose of an electronic digital signature. [2]**
It **confirms the identity** of the person signing (1) and shows that the document **has not been changed** after it was signed (1).

- Thinking that anything on the Internet is **free to use** — most content is protected by copyright automatically.
- Confusing **freeware** (free, closed source) with **open source** (source available, can be modified).
- Saying a trademark protects an invention — it protects a **brand**.
- Listing eGov services without saying what the **benefit** is.
- Thinking an EDS is a picture of your handwritten signature — it is a **cryptographic key**.
